title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across python/ts/go; parity & bump v1.169.0
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: There has been long-standing divergence in how the Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs handle auth header expiry, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming consumption ergonomics. This causes surprising behavior for customers moving between languages and makes SDKs harder to test in parity tests. This PR unifies auth retry behavior, improves streaming ergonomics (reconnect semantics + cancellation), adds parity fixes across implementations, and bumps SDK surface versions to v1.169.0.

What changed (high level):
- Unify auth token refresh behavior: SDKs now fall back to a single well-documented refresh path when an auth error (401/403) is received; refresh is retried with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Standardize retry defaults: idempotent vs non-idempotent categorization aligned across SDKs; default max attempts = 3, initial_backoff = 200ms, max_backoff = 10s, jitter = full.
- Streaming ergonomics: introduce a cancel() / close() method on stream iterators and readable streams set for each SDK. For JS/TS, add AbortSignal support; for Python add context manager + cancel token; Go adds CloseWithError and context propagation. Reconnect logic is explicit and opt-in (auto_reconnect=false by default) to avoid surprising duplicate events.
- Parity fixes: align error kinds and structured error fields for streaming close reasons, and ensure usage examples are identical across SDK READMEs.
- Version bumps: python-sdk v1.169.0, typescript-sdk v1.169.0, go-sdk v1.169.0; changelogs generated.

Detailed changes (single-string description): Implemented unified auth/retry helpers in each SDK repo with shared design doc linked (https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1742/unify-sdks-auth-retry-behavior). Added extensive unit/integration tests that simulate token expiry, transient network errors, and streaming interruptions. TS changes included a small ergonomics shim to preserve backwards compatibility for existing stream consumers. Python changes add a StreamingResponse context manager and ensure synchronous iterators close underlying transport. Go changes add CloseWithError and update several examples. Updated READMEs and migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1742)
- [x] Tests added/updated across SDKs
- [x] Changelogs and README examples updated
- [x] CI green after lint fixes
- [x] Version bumps and package metadata updated

Backwards compatibility notes: Default behaviors change only for new APIs (AbortSignal/cancel/cancel_token). Auto_reconnect remains opt-in to avoid breaking existing consumers. Retry defaults tightened but are configurable via client options. Migration notes in each README show how to keep previous behavior.

Related: Linear ENG-1742, ENG-1743. Support ticket SUP-8891 reported streaming reconnection causing duplicate messages under TLS renegotiation on some Go runtimes.

Merge notes: Small lint issue fixed in a follow-up commit after initial CI failure; final merge via squash once approvals obtained.

tests_summary: Added 34 new unit tests across three SDKs and 6 integration parity tests. Tests cover token refresh on 401, jittered exponential backoff, stream abort/cancel behavior, and reconnect opt-in flow.
release_notes:
- Unify auth token refresh and retry defaults across Python/TS/Go SDKs.
- Add streaming ergonomics: cancel/close APIs and AbortSignal/context support.
- Parity fixes for structured streaming errors.
- SDKs bumped to v1.169.0.
